info.title: Project Browser control-plane API
info.description: Contracts: /v1 prefix, opaque ids, cursor pagination (max 100), If-Match/expected_version optimistic concurrency, Idempotency-Key on lease acquisition, snapshot commit and local workspace import. Authentication: OIDC sign-in in the system browser (Authorization Code + PKCE), then API session tokens (ADR-0013). Authorization: organization role combined with client/profile grants, deny by default; identifiers outside the caller’s reach answer 404 exactly like nonexistent ones.

get.description: Identity provider settings for the desktop sign-in (system browser, Authorization Code + PKCE).

post.description: Enroll this device and start a session with a fresh ID token from the identity provider (used once). Returns the session tokens; keep the refresh token in the OS keychain.

get.description: Devices enrolled for the signed-in account (most recent first, at most 100).

post.description: grant_type=refresh_token rotates the refresh token (presenting a previous one ends the session). grant_type=id_token signs in again on an enrolled device (for example to confirm a sensitive action).
Ends the current session (its refresh token stops working). The device stays enrolled; local data is untouched.

Signs a device out everywhere: its sessions end and it cannot refresh or call the API again until it is enrolled anew. Profiles it had open are released from it (a new fencing token). Local browser data on that device is not deleted (the server cannot reach it).

get.description: Organizations the caller belongs to, with the number of profiles they can see in each. Local workspaces exist only on the device and are not listed.

post.description: Creates an organization with the caller as its owner. Requires a verified e-mail address.

patch.description: Change a member’s role (admin, operator, viewer or billing). Only owners may change an owner’s role; ownership itself moves through /ownership-transfer. Requires If-Match or expected_version.

delete.description: Remove a member (or leave, when it is yourself). Their grants are removed with the membership and their access ends at the next request. The last owner cannot be removed.

post.description: Makes another member an owner and the caller an admin. Requires a sign-in within the last few minutes (REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED otherwise) and the target membership version.
Invite an e-mail address with a role. The token in the response is shown only once; send it to the person. Creating a new invitation for the same address withdraws the previous open one.
Withdraws an open invitation (no effect on one already withdrawn or expired).

get.description: What an invitation link leads to, and whether the signed-in account can accept it.

for_this_account.description: Whether the caller's verified e-mail matches the invitation.

post.description: Join the organization. Single use; refused when expired or withdrawn, and when the signed-in account’s verified e-mail is not the invited address.

patch.description: Rename, recolour or archive. Requires If-Match: "<version>" or body.expected_version.

post.description: Grant a member one client (with all its profiles) or one profile.

patch.description: Changes what a grant allows: launch (open, including uploading the session), edit (configuration) and backup_download (restore). Removing launch from someone who has a profile open ends that session.

get.description: Profiles the caller can see, oldest first; optional name search and client filter.
Configuration export (names, client, notes) of up to 10000 profiles. No browser data or session material. Owners and admins only, after a sign-in within 10 minutes.

post.description: Set the client of, or delete, up to 500 profiles. Each id gets its own outcome; ids outside the caller’s reach report not_found, profiles open on a device report in_use (delete only).

patch.description: Requires If-Match: "<version>" or body.expected_version. Stale versions return 409.

delete.description: Requires If-Match: "<version>". Refused while the profile is open on a device (LEASE_HELD).

post.description: Acquire the profile lease for a device. Requires Idempotency-Key.
Release with the current fencing token. Releasing an already-released lease is a no-op.

get.description: Who has the profile open right now (null: nobody). Uncertain sessions are included.

post.description: Takes the profile for this device (Idempotency-Key required): checks membership, the launch capability, the plan and the browser, then issues a new fencing token. 409 LEASE_HELD while someone has it open; 409 LEASE_UNCERTAIN when the last session ended without closing (ask that person to open the app, or an admin to force a takeover).

Keeps the lease (every 15 s; it lasts 60 s past the last heartbeat) and reports the run state. Returns teammates’ open requests. A holder whose lease expired without anyone else taking it gets it back (revived). 409 FENCING_TOKEN_STALE once it was taken over, revoked or replaced (safe_details.state): stop the browser and keep the local copy aside. 404/403 when access was removed.

Gives the profile back (holder only, current fencing token), optionally with a handoff note for the next person. Allowed after expiry: the holder confirms its browser closed. Releasing twice is a no-op. Open requests for the profile are answered (fulfilled).

Asks the person who has the profile open to hand it over (optional note, no passwords). It never closes their session: they choose when to close and hand off. One open request per person and profile; requests expire after 4 hours.

get.description: Requests for this profile from the last 24 hours, newest first.
The caller’s requests (mine=true) or requests addressed to the caller as holder, from the last 24 hours.

post.description: The person who has the profile open says not now (the requester sees it).
The requester withdraws the request.

Owners and admins end someone’s session or uncertain lease (reason required, confirm: true). A new fencing token fences the old device out: nothing it still sends is written, and its unsynced copy is kept aside on that computer (and as a recovery copy if it uploads one). The other browser may still be open: this cannot stop activity on websites there.

get.description: Uploads kept from devices that lost their session (taken over or revoked), newest first. Owners and admins can restore one as a separate copy; they are erased after the trash period.

One client at a glance: the profiles the caller can see (counts never include hidden ones), who has them open, open tasks, shared bookmarks, and — for owners and admins — who works on it and recent app activity.
Tasks of a client the caller can see, soonest due first (status: open (default), done, all).

post.description: Adds a task. Members with grants add tasks to profiles they can see (or to the whole client with a client grant) and assign them to themselves only. Completing a task never means anything happened on a website.

patch.description: Edits or ticks off a task (If-Match: "<version>").

delete.description: Deletes a task (owners, admins, or whoever created it).

get.description: Shared bookmarks of a client (start-page templates), in their order.

post.description: Adds a shared bookmark (owners and admins): http or https only, at most 50 per client.

patch.description: Renames, re-links or reorders a bookmark (owners and admins; If-Match: "<version>").

get.description: The organization's browser extension policy. Every member's app reads it to judge the extensions installed in organization profiles (off: inventory only; warn; enforce: such profiles open with extensions turned off).

put.description: Replaces the extension policy (owners and admins; If-Match: "<version>").
A device reports the extensions installed in its copy of a profile (names, versions, sources and the permissions they declare; never browsing data). Latest report per profile and device.

get.description: Every extension devices reported in organization profiles: versions, sources, declared permissions (sensitive ones marked), and in how many profiles and devices (owners and admins).

post.description: Starts an encrypted snapshot upload. Requires Idempotency-Key and the live lease. Returns a fresh data key (shown once to this device; a replay of the same request returns the same upload) and upload limits.
Signed URLs (valid 900 s) to upload the named parts of this device's upload. Needs the live lease.

get.description: Parts the storage already holds for this device’s upload (to resume after an interruption).

post.description: Declares the uploaded object (SHA-256, sizes, parts) and hands it to verification (202). Repeating a commit returns the operation as it is. 409 VERSION_CONFLICT when another device committed first.
Cancels this device’s unfinished upload (the profile keeps its last committed snapshot).

get.description: State of one upload (uploading, verifying, committed, failed, canceled, expired).
Committed snapshots of one profile (version history), newest first.

post.description: Authorizes restoring one committed snapshot (default: the newest): a signed download URL and the data key, for this device only. Needs snapshot.restore; every plan is audited.

get.description: Retention, trash period, storage quota and usage of the organization’s snapshots.

patch.description: Changes retention days and the trash period (owners and admins). Quotas are not editable here.

get.description: Deleted profiles that can still be restored, most recently deleted first.

post.description: Restores a deleted profile from the trash (with its snapshots).

get.description: The organization’s key versions (never the keys themselves) and how many snapshots each holds.

post.description: Rotates the organization key (owners; needs a recent sign-in). Existing snapshots are re-wrapped in the background without re-uploading; the old version is destroyed after it is no longer used.
Import a local workspace’s clients and profiles (metadata). dry_run=true returns the plan without changes; dry_run=false requires Idempotency-Key and creates everything atomically.

outcome.description: Organization profiles always get a new server id; the device keeps its local record.
Organization profiles always get a new server id; the device keeps its local record.
